subject: Science
stem: Bacteria and fungi that break down dead plant and animal matter into simpler substances, returning nutrients to the soil, are collectively called:
explanation: Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down dead organic matter, releasing nutrients back into the soil for producers (plants) to use — a vital link in the nutrient cycle.

subject: Science
stem: Storing food in a refrigerator at low temperature helps preserve it for longer mainly because low temperature:

options.option_text: Slows down the growth and activity of microorganisms that cause spoilage
Kills all microorganisms present in the food instantly
Adds preservative chemicals to the food
Removes all water content from the food

explanation: Low temperature slows microbial metabolism and reproduction (it does not kill them outright), which is why refrigerated food lasts longer but still eventually spoils, and why frozen food can be stored much longer still.

subject: Science
stem: Viruses differ fundamentally from bacteria in that viruses:

options.option_text: Can reproduce only inside a living host cell, unlike bacteria which can reproduce independently
Are always beneficial and never cause disease
Are visible with a simple light microscope, unlike bacteria
Are larger in size than bacteria

explanation: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites — they can only replicate by hijacking a living host cell's machinery, unlike bacteria which are independent living cells capable of reproducing on their own given nutrients.
